name: Quilted down outerwear
region: Seattle, the Pacific North-West, and then the world
summary: The jacket that holds a warm cloud of goose down in rows of stitched cells; Eddie Bauer made the first one in Seattle in 1936.

philosophy.core_thesis: Warmth comes from trapped air. Sew the down into baffles that stop it from sliding, and the jacket gives the most heat for the least weight.
design_principles: Sew the cells in rows 8 to 15 cm wide, so that the down cannot move to the bottom.
Fill each cell with 90 to 230 g of goose down, by the cold that the jacket must meet.
Choose a shell of 20 to 70 g per square metre that is tight enough to hold the down.
Bind the cuff and the hem with elastic, to seal the warm air in.
Cut the hood and the collar to close over the chin.
Add a zip with a storm flap that covers the draught.
Stitch each baffle through to a wall, not to the shell, to remove cold spots.
anti_patterns: A thin, loose shell that leaks down
Stitch lines that run through with no baffle wall
A wet, flat jacket that has lost its loft
Bare, uncovered seams at the elbow
A short jacket that leaves the kidney bare

silhouette.shape: A round, padded jacket with horizontal or vertical rows of puffed cells, a high collar and a snug cuff.
silhouette.line: A rounded, soft shoulder, a body that puffs in rows and a hem at the hip.
silhouette.fit: Roomy over a jumper; the elastic cuff and hem keep the warm air in.
silhouette.proportion: Jacket to the hip bone or to the thigh; roughly 1 to 1.2 chest to hip with the fill.
rules: Divide the body into baffles in even rows.
Put a high collar and a fixed or a rolled hood on the jacket.
Close the cuff and the hem with elastic or a drawcord.
Cover the zip with a flap held by studs.
Keep a pocket at the chest and at the hip, lined with brushed cloth.

fabrics.rule: Choose a light, tight shell of cotton poplin or ripstop nylon, and fill it with goose down. The down gives the warmth, the shell holds it.

methods: goose down fill in each cell
storm flap over the front zip
quilted stitch lines through two layers
construction.closures: A full-length zip with a storm flap, stud snaps over the flap, and a drawcord at the hem.
construction.details: A baffled body, a high collar, a hood with a drawcord, two hand pockets and a chest pocket.

surface.pattern: Plain colour in horizontal or vertical baffles; the stitch lines make the pattern.
surface.gloss: A matte shell at 5–15 GU; a polished nylon shell at 40–80 GU.
surface.wear: The loft falls with wet and with crush; the owner washes and tumbles the jacket to bring the down back.

palette.strategy: A single saturated or dark colour, which the baffles show in light and shade.

processes: cutting of the shell and the wall cloth
sewing of the baffles by machine
weighing and blowing in of the down
closing of each cell and bar tack
making.scale: Made by hand in a Seattle shop from 1936; made in the thousand by factories from the 1950s and by the million today.
making.signs: Even rows of puffed baffles, a high collar, an elastic cuff, and a tight shell that holds the down.

pieces.form: Hip-length jacket with horizontal box baffles and a high collar
Sleeveless down vest with vertical baffles
Early jacket with a cotton shell and sewn baffles
Long hooded parka with a down fill and a storm flap

emotion.target_response: A warm, soft sense of safety against the cold: the wearer looks padded, round and snug.

use_cases: a product brief for a winter jacket line
an image prompt for a cold-weather scene
a costume brief for a 1950s climbing film
avoid_when: the brief is a tailored city coat
the brief is a hot-weather look
the brief wants a slim, flat line

modifiers.how: Drop the baffles to a thin quilt, use a twill shell and add a plain, deep hood.
Use a thinner ripstop shell, a slim cut and add a laminated hard shell over it.

ornament_level.note: The baffle rows are the only decoration; colour blocking adds more.
